what_it_does: A water-binding humectant that helps skin feel hydrated and plumper.
summary_short: Sodium hyaluronate is the salt form of hyaluronic acid, used in skincare to attract and hold water on the skin. It is widely used as a skin-conditioning ingredient and was considered safe in cosmetics at concentrations up to 2%.
summary_long:
Sodium hyaluronate is a salt form of hyaluronic acid, a naturally occurring water-binding polymer found in skin and connective tissue. In skincare, it acts mainly as a humectant: it helps draw water into the outer layers of skin, improving temporary hydration, softness, and the look of plumpness.

The strongest skincare-relevant evidence here is a cosmetic safety review covering hyaluronic acid, sodium hyaluronate, and potassium hyaluronate. The review states that these ingredients function as skin-conditioning agents in cosmetics at concentrations up to 2%, and concluded they are safe for cosmetic use as described [PMID:unknown].

Safety data in the review were reassuring: hyaluronic acid was not toxic across multiple animal toxicity studies, was not genotoxic, was not a sensitizer in animal studies, and was not considered a reproductive or developmental toxicant [PMID:unknown]. Widespread clinical use, mostly through injection rather than topical skincare, was also reported to be free of significant adverse reactions.

Sodium hyaluronate is commonly paired with other hydrating and barrier-supporting ingredients, such as glycerin, panthenol, ceramides, and lightweight emollients. It has no major ingredient conflicts in everyday skincare use, but humectants work best when paired with a moisturizer that helps reduce water loss, especially in dry environments.

One related meta-analysis looked at sodium hyaluronate eye drops for xerophthalmia, or dry eyes. It found that sodium hyaluronate may help relieve dry-eye symptoms, but did not clearly outperform other eye drops or therapies [PMID:unknown]. That evidence supports its water-binding, lubricating role, though it is not direct proof of facial skincare results.
quick_facts: Reported safe in cosmetics up to 2%
